summary: A memory-and-ABI release: byte vectors use packed slots, arm64 contracts compile, and the first non-Vec ownership slice drops bound strings.

highlights.title: Borrowed and moved vectors are reclaimed
highlights.text: Fresh vectors passed by reference to ordinary functions, or moved into a struct literal, stay owned by the caller and are freed at scope exit. Constructors that return a struct use the owns-return contract; the editor frame path no longer grows per frame.

highlights.title: arm64 contracts compile
highlights.text: The contract evaluator loads a Result payload with its real field type, so Result[Str, Error] contracts no longer fail LLVM verification on arm64. The arm64 packaging gate is unblocked.

highlights.title: Inline Result payload indices
highlights.text: An inline Result.value[i] in a concatenation now reads the element's real type instead of formatting its pointer bits. The bound workaround is no longer needed.

highlights.title: Bound strings are reclaimed
highlights.text: Freshly built local strings from concatenation and numeric formatting are freed at scope exit. String-heavy loops no longer grow per iteration; Map, JSON, and HTTP follow.

highlights.title: Packed Vec slot stride for byte buffers
highlights.text: Vec.with_len, push, reserve, shrink_to_fit and insert use the header elem_size (with the legacy 8-byte fallback) instead of a hardcoded 8. Vec[UInt8], Vec[Bool] and Vec[Char] become packed; with_len reads v.elem_size on the type receiver. A 4 MiB with_len byte buffer fits a 24 MiB cap in the combined compiler tree.

highlights.title: HTTP/2 primitive layer
highlights.text: The pure h2 primitives add the RFC 7541 dynamic table, the full Huffman codec (H=1 string decode/encode), and HEADERS plus CONTINUATION reassembly. These are standalone helpers; the connection state machine is not included.

known_issues: Map, JSON enum-tree, and HTTP request buffers still retain; the next retention slices cover them.
Strings returned from functions are not yet dropped; only fresh local bindings are.
Microcontroller targets use a bump allocator and do not support exceptions.
